newsitem.title: USA: Rhone-Poulenc says Synercid NDA delayed.
newsitem.headline: Rhone-Poulenc says Synercid NDA delayed.

text.p: Rhone-Poulenc Rorer Inc said Thursday that the New Drug Application (NDA) filing date for Synercid has been delayed pending an inspection of the manufacturing site by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration.
The company said it expects the NDA to be filed during the second half of 1997.
Synercid, an investigational antibiotic, is to be manufactured at Centeon LLC's Kankakee site, the company said. Centeon is a joint venture with Hoechst AG.
A company spokesman said the NDA was earlier projected for filing at the end of 1996.
The company also said it has decided to halt the clinical development program for its fananserin drug because of its lack of efficacy as a potential treatment for schizophrenia.
The drug was in the Phase II trial stage, according to a company spokesman.

Rhone-Poulenc Rorer, which is the U.S. based pharmaceutical subsidiary of Rhone-Poulenc SA, reported first quarter earnings on Thursday of $0.41 per share on net sales of $1.09 billion, compared with $0.55 a share on net sales of $1.27 billion in the prior-year period.
It said its results were hurt by a slightly negative contribution by its Centeon joint venture, as well as wholesaler buying patterns in the United States and weakness in the European markets.

The divestiture of several products during 1996 caused sales in the first quarter to decline by nine percentage points, and the strong dollar reduced sales by a further six percentage points, the company said.
However, the company said, based on the incremental contribution of new products, it sees sales growth of five to six percent on a comparable basis for all of 1997.
